text:
Marathon Petroleum's stock ticked up 0.74% today to $364.94, extending a two-week gain of 2.4%. The move reflects ongoing geopolitical tension in the Middle East—specifically around the Strait of Hormuz, a critical chokepoint for global oil shipments—combined with strong refinery utilization at 97.4% and tightening energy supplies globally, particularly in Europe. These conditions typically support refined product margins and fuel demand for refiners.

The broader backdrop matters: U.S. oil is trading at $83.90 per barrel while world oil sits higher at $88.24, signaling supply concerns abroad. With European gas storage historically low heading into winter and Middle East LNG flows disrupted, global energy markets remain tight, which tends to lift margins for U.S. refiners who can sell refined products into those constrained markets. The de-escalation talk from Qatar and ongoing geopolitical uncertainty keep the risk premium in energy prices intact.
